metadata.title: [FEATURE]: Propagate backing MCP server `instructions` to clients
metadata.author: kimsehwan96

description:
### 🧭 Type of Feature Please select the most appropriate category: - [x] Enhancement to existing functionality - [ ] New feature or capability - [ ] New MCP-compliant server - [ ] New component or integration - [ ] Developer tooling or test improvement - [ ] Packaging, automation and deployment (ex: pypi, docker, quay.io, kubernetes, terraform) - [ ] Other (please describe below) ### 🧭 Epic **Title:** Expose backing-server `instructions` through the gateway's `initialize` response **Goal:** Let LLM clients see the operational hints that each federated MCP server provides about how to use its tools, resources, and prompts. Today these hints are dropped at the gateway boundary. **Why now:** Federated gateways become more useful as backing servers grow in number and complexity. The `instructions` channel is the place where upstream maintainers communicate non-obvious usage guidance (e.g. "always paginate", "tool descriptions reference the authenticated user's id", "use search before fetching"). Losing that information to the LLM degrades tool-use quality even when everything else (auth, tool list, schemas) is correctly federated. ### Background — What `instructions` is The MCP spec defines `instructions` as an optional string in the `InitializeResult` response. From the spec: > "Instructions describing how to use the server and its features. This can be used by clients to improve the LLM's understanding of available tools, resources, etc. It can be thought of like a 'hint' to the model. For example, this information MAY be added to the system prompt." So it is a server's chance to give the LLM a system-prompt-level hint about how to use its capabilities. It is a separate channel from per-tool `description`. ### Background — Current Context Forge behavior When a client opens a session against the gateway, the `initialize` response Context Forge returns has a hardcoded literal in the `instructions` field — something like `"ContextForge providing federated tools, resources and prompts. Use /admin interface for configuration."` — regardless of what the backing servers actually advertise. Backing-server `instructions` are not captured, not stored, and not forwarded. ```mermaid flowchart LR C[Client / LLM] -- initialize --> G[ContextForge] G -- initialize --> A[Backing server A] G -- initialize --> B[Backing server B] A -- instructions: 'use LIMIT on big tables' --> G B -- instructions: 'page IDs are hierarchical' --> G G -- "instructions: 'ContextForge providing federated tools...'" --> C G -. dropped .-> X((upstream
instructions)) ``` --- ### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 1 **As a:** an LLM-application developer using ContextForge to federate multiple MCP servers **I want:** the operational guidance that each backing server provides via `instructions` to reach my model **So that:** my agent makes better tool-use decisions without me re-typing or summarizing each server's hints into my own system prompt #### ✅ Acceptance Criteria ```gherkin Scenario: Backing-server hints reach the client Given a virtual server federates two backing MCP servers And each backing server returns a non-empty `instructions` value at initialize When a client opens a session against the gateway Then the gateway's `initialize` response carries those instructions to the client And the relationship between each instruction and its source server is recognizable Scenario: Backing server has no instructions Given a backing server returns no `instructions` field When a client opens a session against the gateway Then that backing server contributes nothing to the gateway's `instructions` value And the gateway behaves as if that server's hints field is empty ``` --- ### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 2 **As a:** ContextForge operator **I want:** the gateway to keep something sensible in `instructions` even if backing servers don't supply one, and let me override the result if it doesn't read well in production **So that:** I can curate the LLM-facing hint without having to fork the gateway #### ✅ Acceptance Criteria ```gherkin Scenario: No backing server provides instructions Given no backing server contributes an `instructions` value When a client opens a session against the gateway Then the gateway falls back to a reasonable default (today's hardcoded literal is fine as a default) Scenario: Operator provides an override Given an operator has explicitly set an instructions value for a virtual server When a client opens a session against the gateway Then the operator's value is returned instead of the auto-merged backing-server values ``` --- ### 📐 Design Sketch (optional) I'm intentionally not prescribing a specific implementation — the right shape (in-memory cache vs. DB column, merge format, override surface) seems like a maintainer call. Possible directions I've seen referenced or used elsewhere: - Auto-merge: capture each backing server's instructions at federation time, concatenate with per-server labels at `initialize` time (this is the shape LiteLLM's MCP gateway uses today) - Operator override: a per-virtual-server field that wins over the auto-merge when set - Tool-description prefix: prepend each tool's description with its server's instructions (decentralized but can bloat context) --- ### 🔗 MCP Standards Check - [x] Change adheres to current [MCP specifications](https://developer.ibm.com/tutorials/awb-handle-remote-tool-calling-model-context-protocol/) - [x] No breaking changes to existing MCP-compliant integrations - [ ] If deviations exist, please describe them below: --- ### 🔄 Alternatives Considered - Leaving the current behavior as-is and asking each agent-application developer to manually summarize backing-server hints into their own system prompt. Works but does not scale as the number of federated servers grows. - Tool-description prefix only (no `instructions` merging). Works for tool-related hints but is repetitive and bypasses the `instructions` channel that the spec defines for exactly this purpose. --- ### 📓 Additional Context - MCP spec — `InitializeResult.instructions` definition: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle
